sections.heading: Phase-shift to power mapping
sections.text: The relationship between phase shift and power is nonlinear (sinusoidal). Near phi=0, the sensitivity dP/dphi is low. Near phi=pi/2, sensitivity is high. The PI controller must handle this gain variation across the operating range.

sections.heading: Bandwidth
sections.text: Set the voltage-loop crossover at fsw/20 to fsw/10. The plant is essentially a first-order system (L filters the power transfer), so a simple PI works well. Start with kp ~ 2*pi*f_crossover*L_series/Vout.

sections.heading: Bidirectional handover
sections.text: When the power reference crosses zero, the phase-shift command must cross zero smoothly. Anti-windup reset at phi=0 prevents the integrator from stalling on the wrong side. Implement a dead-band around phi=0 to prevent chattering.

sections.heading: Gain direction
sections.text: Increasing kp improves transient response but may cause phase-shift overshoot (the output oscillates around the target). If the phase-shift command oscillates, reduce kp. For steady-state error, increase ki — but watch for integrator windup at the phase-shift limits.
